summary_ltne: **Reading.** With the same apertures the dual-continuum model cools the 16B bottom hole by -5.6 (-11.6 to -0.4) °C, which halves the misfit (+11.2 → +5.5 (+0.1 to +11.1) °C). But it also leaves cold, viscous water near 16A, and the injector pressure rises from 42.2 to 48.5 MPa (measured 42.85). Refitted to the August pressures (apertures × 1.13), it holds the pressure (42.3 MPa) and leaves a misfit of **+4.5 (-2.2 to +10.8) °C**. So local thermal non-equilibrium explains a little over half of the last 11 °C. The rest is the size of the temperature-model bias that section 4 finds at 16B (about +6 °C). Over 30 years at 10 kg/s the refitted model ends -3.1 (-6.0 to -1.4) °C cooler than the equilibrium model (6 members); the first 5 % cooling arrives after 0.46 (0.21 to 0.89) years instead of 1.77 (1.10 to 2.55): thin, fast paths cool first, the bulk of the heat is unchanged.
summary_front: **Reading: the correction fails the rule set in advance.** It removes most of the scatter (KAI, 10 kg/s: raw +54 (-26 to +115) % → corrected -20 (-24 to -13) %), but it leaves the corrected breakthrough 10–20 % early, and the 10 kg/s median misses the 15 % limit. The bias has one sign, so a calibrated factor may pass, but it would have to be tested on members it was not fitted to. Until then the case page states only the 30-year heat for coarse models.
summary_shmin: **Reading.** The result turns on the minifracs' cooling adjustment. As measured (0.60 psi/ft) the limit at 16A is 32.2 MPa, lower than the August test's 42.9 MPa, and no member can run 10 kg/s. With the report's mid adjustment (0.80 psi/ft) the highest rate is 11.8 (11.6 to 12.3) kg/s, and with the high one 16.2 (15.8 to 16.9) kg/s, against 9.6 (9.3 to 10.2) kg/s with GDR 1222. A minifrac in the reservoir section of 16A would settle it.
summary_geotherm: **Reading.** The temperature model is about +6 °C too hot at the gauge (-11 to +9 °C; at most +12 °C, against the last quiet reading). That is the size of what is left of the produced-temperature misfit after the dual-continuum model (section 1). The model was checked against 58-32 in notebook 1 (1.7 °C); at 16B, 300 m away, it may be a little hot. A static log in 16B over the open interval would test this directly.
